texts.preamble: Smt. B.N.A. Shilpa Lakshmi vs ) Sri B.N. Nitin Kumar on 29 June, 2018 In The Court Of The Metropolitan Magistrate Traffic Court - Iv, Bangalore Present: Gayathri.S.Kate, B.com, Llb., Mmtc - Iv, Bangalore Dated : This The 29Th Day Of June 2018 Crl.Misc.No.119/2013 Petitioner: Smt. B.N.A. Shilpa Lakshmi, W/o. Sri B.N. Nitin Kumar, Age: 31 years, R/at Flat No.103, C Block, Majestic Residency, Tavarkere Main Road, Bangalore - 560 029 Vs . Respondent: 1) Sri B.N. Nitin Kumar, S/o. B.R. Nagaraj, Age: 34 years 2) Sri B.R. Nagaraj, S/o. Boggaram Ramalinga Shetty, Age: 60 years 3) Smt. B.N. Rashmi, S/o. B.R. Nagaraj, Age: 54 years,
texts.facts: 1 This is a petition filed by the petitioner U/s.12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 seeking relief's U/s.18, 19, 20 and 22 of the said Act. 2. The case of the petitioner in brief is as under: It is the case of the petitioner that the petitioner and 1st respondent are Hindus and their families are related. The aggrieved person's maternal home is at Vishakapatnam, Andhra Pradesh. The proposal of the 1st respondent was brought the 1st respondent's maternal grandfather in the early part of 2003. The families of the aggrieved person and the 1st respondent along with aggrieved person and 1st respondent met in Hyderabad in August 2013 to discuss the marriage proposal and the alliance was fixed. However the respondents 1 to 3 made an exorbitant dowry demand and finally the aggrieved person's family was constrained to agree to pay a dowry of Rs.61,00,000/- in various forms to the respondent. It is submitted that since the families of the aggrieved person and respondents were related, the aggrieved person's father was constrained to agree to the dowry demand fearing breakdown in the family relations. After the marriage alliance was fixed, the respondents 1 to 3 called the aggrieved person and her family informing them that the 1st respondent had got a seat in Oxford, London and hence the marriage had to be performed before he left United Kingdom. As such the aggrieved person's parents and the aggrieved person came to Bangalore in August 2003 to finalize the marriage date and other details. At that time, 1st respondent and his parents demanded that the residential flat in Vishakapatnam standing in the name of the aggrieved person's father should be transferred to their name as consideration of the marriage. At that time the said flat was worth around Rs.15,00,000/-. Though the aggrieved person's father was not keen to transfer it to their name, it was agreed that the same would be transferred into the aggrieved person's name. The marriage was fixed on 8th September 2003 at ISCKON Bangalore and all arrangements and expenses for the same were borne by the aggrieved person's father. This was also one of the conditions imposed by the respondents 1 to 3 as a condition for agreeing to go ahead with the marriage. The respondents 1 to 3 had also demanded a sum of Rs.4,00,000/- for the purchase of a car, The aggrieved person's father gave the respondents 1 to 3 a sum of Rs.14,00,000/- and another amount of Rs.10,00,000/- (Rupees ten lakhs only) by cash for purchase of gold. That apart, the aggrieved person's parents also incurred expenditure for purchase of gold and jewelry to be given to the respondents and their relations. The aggrieved person and 1st respondent were married as per Hindu rites and customs on 8th September 2003 at ISCKON Bangalore and the same was registered under the provisions of the Hindu marriage Act on 15th September 2003 before the Registrar of Marriages, Jayanagar, Bangalore. The copy of the marriage certificate and the wedding photograph is produced herewith as Document No 4 and 5. As stated earlier all the expenses for the marriage was borne by the aggrieved person's father. The aggrieved person's father incurred the entire expenses of around Rs.10,00,000/- for the conduct of the marriage. The 1st respondent went to Chennai for his interview but for some reason not disclosed to the aggrieved person, his visa was rejected. The aggrieved person and 1st respondent then left for the reception in Vishakaptnam. It is submitted Smt. B.N.A. Shilpa Lakshmi vs ) Sri B.N. Nitin Kumar on 29 June, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129173256/ 2 that as demanded by the respondents 1 to 3 the aggrieved person's father had to make arrangements for the honeymoon to Singapore and Malaysia. Since the aggrieved person's father did not want the aggrieved person to undergo any discomfort in her matrimonial home, he arranged for the honeymoon to Singapore and Malaysia by incurring an expenditure of around Rs.2,40,000/- (Rupees two lakhs forty thousand only). After the aggrieved person and 1st respondent returned from the reception, they left for their honeymoon in November 2003. During the honeymoon, the 1st respondent would constantly lei to the aggrieved person on trivial issues and would pick up flights on trivial issues. However since the aggrieved person was newly married, she chose to ignore these incidents hoping that things will improve after they settle down to lead a marital life. The aggrieved person and 1st respondent returned to the matrimonial home in Bangalore at Jayanagar and started living with respondents 2 and 3. Meanwhile there was a robbery and matrimonial house was burnt. The 3rd respondent claimed that all the jewelry given to the petitioner at the time of the marriage worth Rs.10,00,000/- Was stolen in the said robbery. After the said incident, the aggrieved person and respondents 1 to 3 shifted to a rented house in Jayanagar. The aggrieved person's nightmare started as the respondents 1 to 3 would constantly shout and harass the aggrieved person for all trivial issues and would constantly come up with new monetary and dowry demands. This continued for nearly a year and added to this harassment was the fact that the 1st respondent had left his job for joining Oxford and since the Oxford seat did not come through remained at home without a job for nearly one year. The aggrieved person realized that she was pregnant around January 2004 and since she had medical complications, she was advised bed rest for the entire term of the pregnancy. The respondents 1 to 3 insisted that they could not look after the aggrieved person and demanded that the aggrieved person's mother join them to look after the aggrieved person for some time. However after few days, the aggrieved person's mother left, the harassment meted out by the 3rd respondent increased and it also lead to fights in the family. The 3rd respondent claimed that she was angry with the 1st respondent and demanded that the aggrieved person and the 1st respondent leave the matrimonial home. The aggrieved person's parents had to come from Vishakapatnam and had to take the aggrieved person and the 1st respondent to Vishakapatnam as they did not have any place to stay. Meanwhile the 1st respondent secured a job in Hyderabad at TATA teleservices and consequently the aggrieved person and 1st respondent moved to Hyderabad. However the 3rd respondent was not happy with the said move and started harassing the aggrieved person over phone and instigating the 1st respondent, who would then harass and torture the aggrieved person. At her insistence, the aggrieved person and 1st respondent were compelled to move back to Bangalore. The 3rd respondent also took away the money given as dowry and claimed that she needed the same for making investments. The aggrieved person gave birth to a baby girl on 16.09.2004 who was named Shruthi. The copy of the birth certificate is produced herewith as Document No.6. The entire expenses for the delivery and birth of the child was borne by the aggrieved person's father with no contribution from the respondents 1 to 3. After a few days of the birth of the minor child, the 1st respondent came back to Bangalore and the aggrieved person also joined the 1st respondent with the infant in Bangalore. Unmindful of the fact that the aggrieved person had just recently given birth to a child, the respondents 1 to 3 would physically torture the aggrieved person by making her stand on bed for hours. The 3rd respondent would constantly abuse and torture the aggrieved person apart from insulting the aggrieved person and her parents. The respondents 1 to 3 were unhappy that the aggrieved person had given birth to a Smt. B.N.A. Shilpa Lakshmi vs ) Sri B.N. Nitin Kumar on 29 June, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129173256/ 3 baby girl. All this while keeping in mind the relationship in the family, the aggrieved person put up with the torture and harassment meted out to her. The respondents 1 to 3 decided to buy a flat bearing No.103, C Block in Majestic Residency, Bangalore and to meet this demand demanded that the aggrieved person contribute money by asking the same from her father. The aggrieved person's father had deposited money in fixed deposits in the name of the 1st respondent for Rs.10,00,000/- The respondent and his parents used up the said fixed deposits and another sum of Rs.9,61,000/- invested in the aggrieved person's name by her father and the amount of Rs.4,00,000/- given at the time of the marriage for purchase of a car to pay the down payment for the flat at Majestic Residency. Though the respondents 1 to 3 had not contributed any major amount, the said flat was purchased in the joint names of the aggrieved person and 1st respondent.. The respondent availed a loan of Rs.26,00,000/- for the purchase of the said house. The loan agreement is produced herewith as Document No.9. The aggrieved person was continuously harassed and tortured for more money and finally unable to bear the harassment and torture the aggrieved person left the matrimonial home and went back to her parent's house in Vishakapatnam with her child in 2006. The aggrieved person's parents brought the aggrieved person back and counseled the 1st respondent to take care of the aggrieved person and the minor child. In 2006 the flat in Vishakapatnam was sold for Rs.18,00,000/- (Rupees eighteen lakhs only) and the respondents 1 to 3 took away the entire money claiming that they would use the same to buy another flat. The respondents 1 to 3 also claimed that the EMI amount on the loan would be cleared from the money given by the aggrieved person's father to them. Thus, the respondents 1 to 3 have not contributed a single rupee for the flat where the aggrieved person is residing at present. In 2007 the aggrieved person and the respondents 1 to 3 moved into the BTM house where the 1st respondent is at present residing. The respondents 1 to 3 continued to harass and torture the aggrieved person. Things started deteriorating day by day and the aggrieved person's married life was becoming a hell. The respondents 1 to 3 would constantly abuse her and harass her and blame her for every trivial issue unrelated to her. The aggrieved person would not be allowed to watch TV or be given proper food. The respondents 1 to 3 would use every opportunity to humiliate the aggrieved person in social and public circles. Once again unable to bear the torture and harassment the aggrieved person returned to her parent's house who brought her back and tried to counsel the 1st respondent. In the year 2008, the aggrieved person and 1st respondent decided to move into the flat at Majestic Residency. The aggrieved person went around to get the interiors and the furniture done and supervise the work being done and all this time, the respondents 1 to 3 would demand that the aggrieved person's family bear the expenditure for the same. The aggrieved person's father paid all the money for the furniture etc since he wanted to ensure that the aggrieved person's marital life would go on smoothly. Finally they moved into the flat in December 2008 and even at the time of the puja the 1st respondent did not turn up for the grihapravesh puja and the aggrieved person's parents had to sit for the puja instead of the aggrieved person and 1st respondent. The respondents 1 to 3 resented the aggrieved person getting involved in the apartment complex activities. They would use every opportunity to humiliate the aggrieved person and belittle her and would abuse and shout at the aggrieved person in public. On one occasion in August 2010, the 1st respondent hit the aggrieved person with his slippers. The respondents 2 and 3 were also present and they instigated and egged the 1st respondent to hit the aggrieved person. The 3rd respondent would constantly come to the aggrieved person and 1st respondent's house and abuse the aggrieved person and create fights consequent to which the 1st respondent would get abusive with the aggrieved person. The 3rd respondent would come and start Smt. B.N.A. Shilpa Lakshmi vs ) Sri B.N. Nitin Kumar on 29 June, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129173256/ 4 poisoning the mind of the minor daughter against the aggrieved person. The 1st respondent would start controlling how much time the aggrieved person spent with whom and where she could go. The aggrieved person was thus a virtual prisoner in the house with the 1st respondent controlling all her movements. This harassment and torture went on for years and even continues as on date. The 1st respondent would pick up fights on trivial issues, abuse the aggrieved person and would then of and stay with his parents. He would resent any demand for money for household expenses and even money to celebrate the minor daughter's birthday. The 1st respondent would prevent the aggrieved person from inviting any friends and children for the minor daughter's birthday and would threaten to create a scene and abuse guests if the aggrieved person invited any one for the birthday or even had a birthday party. However things turned dangerous when in December 2011, the aggrieved person came to know that the 1st respondent had been video taping the aggrieved person while she was having bath or changing clothes. The 1st respondent started spiking the aggrieved person's tea and medicines with sleeping pills and would molest and film the aggrieved person without her knowledge and consent. When the aggrieved person confronted the 1st respondent, the 1st respondent physically assaulted the aggrieved person in the presence of the servant and after a heated argument went to stay with his parents. The aggrieved person's father once again came and tried to counsel him and the 1st respondent promised to change and even confessed to having video taped the aggrieved person while she was bathing and administering her sleeping pills without her knowledge. The 1st respondent would constantly call up relations and aggrieved person's parents and threaten that he would divorce the aggrieved person. In the year 2012, the 3rd respondent started announcing that she was getting the 1st respondent married to another woman and that they would get rid of the aggrieved person in one way or the other. However the said harassment and torture by the respondents 1 to 3 have increased once again in the past six months. They have been threatening to cause the aggrieved person and the minor child grievous physical harm. In the third week of May 2013, the respondents 1 and 3 claimed that the 1st respondent had attempted suicide and that they would register a false criminal case against the aggrieved person and his parents. It is pertinent to state here that the 1st respondent has been living with his parents since several months and the aggrieved person has reason to believe that the said action and attempts are to threaten and intimidate the aggrieved person. The 1st respondent has also threatened to stop paying the EMI amount of Rs.31,000/- for the house to coerce the aggrieved person's father to pay the same. It is pertinent to state that the respondents 1 to 3 while working out the accounts during their illegal demands for more dowry have informed the aggrieved person that only Rs.59,40,000 has been paid to them so far from the agreed Rs.61,00,000/-. On 24th May 2013, the 1st respondent tried to come into the aggrieved person's house claiming to come with the police with the sole intention of threatening and harassing the aggrieved person and snatching the minor child away. The respondent 2 and 3 have also called up the aggrieved person's parents and the aggrieved person and threatened that they would throw the aggrieved person out of the said flat and file false criminal cases against the aggrieved person and her parents. The aggrieved person then approached the jurisdictional police to file a complaint against the respondents on 26.5.2013. While filing the complaint, the aggrieved person was informed that the 1st respondent had filed a complaint against the aggrieved person on 15th May 2013 making false allegations that the aggrieved person was harassing the 1st respondent. The minor child is studying in the 3rd standard in Sudarshan Vidya Mandir, Jayanagar, Bangalore. The aggrieved person was constrained to file a GWC 107/2013 seeking guardianship and custody of the child as the aggrieved person feared that the respondents Smt. B.N.A. Shilpa Lakshmi vs ) Sri B.N. Nitin Kumar on 29 June, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129173256/ 5 may come and snatch the child away. The Hon'ble Family Court by an order dated 3.6.2013 was pleased to grant an ex-parte injunction. The aggrieved person has been harassed and tortured physically and mentally by the respondents 1 to 3 since 2003 and continue to be harassed even as on date. The harassment and torture continue despite having met all their illegal dowry demands. The aggrieved person has been subjected to cruelty both physical and mental by the respondents 1 to 3 making it impossible for the aggrieved person to stay with the 1st respondent and lead a marital life. The physical assault, attempts of suicide, filming the aggrieved person, spiking her tea and medicines are all acts of cruelty which makes is impossible for the aggrieved person to live with the 1st respondent. The aggrieved person has been a victim of domestic violence in the hands of the respondent No.1 to 3. The aggrieved person fears safety to her life of the minor daughter. It is submitted that the aggrieved person has thus been a victim of mental verbal and physical abuse and cruelty in the hands of the 1st respondent. The aggrieved person has been a victim of domestic violence in the hands of all the respondents. The respondents No.1 to 3 have subjected the aggrieved person to physical abuse, sexual abuse, verbal and emotional abuse and economic abuse. It is prayed that the Hon'ble Court may take cognizance of the complaint and pass all of the orders deemed necessary in the circumstances of the case. (a) Pass protection orders U/s.18 and (b) Pass residence orders U/s.19 and (c) Direct the 1st respondents to pay monetary relief U/s.20 and (d) Direct the respondents to grant compensation or damages U/s.22 and (e) Pass such interim orders as the court deems jus and proper (f) Pass any orders as deems fit in the circumstances of the case. Orders required : (i) protection order U/s.18, Prohibiting acts of domestic violence by granting an injunction against respondents from repeating any of the acts mentioned in this application. Prohibiting the respondents from entering the workplace and residence of the aggrieved person. Prohibiting the respondents from entering the school or any other place frequented by the minor child. Prohibiting any form of communication by the respondents with the aggrieved person. Smt. B.N.A. Shilpa Lakshmi vs ) Sri B.N. Nitin Kumar on 29 June, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129173256/ 6 Prohibiting alienation of assets by the respondents. Directing the respondents to stay away from the dependents / relatives / any other person of the aggrieved person to prohibit violence against them. (ii) Residence order U/s.19: An order restraining the respondents from: Preventing the aggrieved staying in the home at Flat No.103, C Block, Majestic Residency, Tavarkere main road, Bangalore. Entering the Flat No.103, C Block, Majestic Residency, Tavarkere Main Road, Bangalore where the aggrieved person resides there. Direct the 1st respondent to continue paying the EMI towards the house loan on the property viz Flat No.103, C Block, Majestic Residency, Tavarkere Main Road, Bangalore. Alienating / disposing / encumbering the shared household. (a) Under the Hindu Marriage Act, 1956 Sections 13(1)(ia) being M.C. No.2119/13 pending in the 4th Addl. Prl. Family Court, Bangalore. (b) Guardian and Wards Case in GWC No.107/13 on the file of the Family Judge, Bangalore. WHEREFORE it is most respectfully prayed that this Hon'ble Court be pleased to grant the reliefs claimed therein and pass such orders as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper under the given facts and circumstances of the case for protecting the aggrieved person from domestic violence and in the interest of justice. 3. After registration of the case, summons was issued to the respondents and they appeared through their counsel and filed detailed statement of objection denying each and every allegations made against them. 4. In order to substantiate their respective contentions, the petitioner got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked 11 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.11. The respondent got examined himself as R.W.1 and got marked 22 documents as Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.22.
